question: A biotech receives a £50m milestone payment from a partner when a drug reaches Phase 3. Walk me through the statements, and say how you would treat it in analysis.
model_answer_md:
Assuming the milestone has been earned — the trigger event has occurred and there is no further obligation — it is recognised immediately.

**Income statement.** Revenue +£50m. At 25 % tax that is £12.5m, so net income rises **£37.5m**. For a company that was loss-making, this may be the first profitable period it has ever reported.

**Cash flow statement.** Net income +£37.5m, with nothing to add back, so cash rises **£37.5m** — the £50m received less the £12.5m tax. (In practice accumulated losses often shelter the tax, in which case cash rises the full £50m.)

**Balance sheet.** Cash +£37.5m, retained earnings +£37.5m. **Balances.**

**In analysis I would normalise it out.** It is a one-off, non-recurring receipt tied to a single event. Leaving it in makes the company look profitable and makes any earnings multiple meaningless, because next year there will be no milestone.
key_points: Cash +£37.5m — the receipt less tax (or the full £50m if losses shelter it)
One-off and non-recurring: normalise it out of underlying earnings
Leaving it in makes earnings multiples meaningless

follow_ups.question: What if milestones are received every year?
follow_ups.answer_md: Then the judgement changes. If a company has a broad partnered portfolio producing milestones regularly, some level of milestone income is arguably part of its recurring business model — though it is still lumpy and unpredictable. I would look at several years, take a normalised average rather than any single year, and be explicit that it is an estimate.

follow_ups.question: How does it affect valuation multiples?
follow_ups.answer_md: It distorts anything earnings-based. A P/E built on a milestone year is meaningless — the earnings are non-recurring, so the multiple looks absurdly low and reverts the following year. For pre-commercial biotech this is one reason valuation leans on risk-adjusted NPV of the pipeline rather than on multiples at all.

weak_answer_note: Treats the milestone as recurring revenue, or forgets tax and reports cash up the full £50m without noting the assumption.
